components.css: .ds-card { background: #fff; border: 1px solid #E7E1D4; border-radius: 1.125rem; padding: 24px; max-width: 340px; box-shadow: 0 1px 0 0 rgba(23,19,14,0.04), 0 10px 30px -18px rgba(23,19,14,0.28); transition: transform 220ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), box-shadow 220ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-card:hover { transform: translateY(-4px); box-shadow: 0 1px 0 0 rgba(23,19,14,0.05), 0 26px 60px -26px rgba(23,19,14,0.40); } .ds-card-readout { font-family: SFMono-Regular, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.72rem; letter-spacing: 0.04em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #C22F0A; margin: 0 0 8px; } .ds-card-title { font-family: 'Bricolage Grotesque', sans-serif; font-weight: 800; font-size: 1.25rem; letter-spacing: -0.02em; color: #17130E; margin: 0 0 6px; } .ds-card-body { font-family: 'Hanken Grotesk', sans-serif; font-size: 0.9375rem; line-height: 1.65; color: #423B32; margin: 0; }

components.name: Beacon Pin
components.description: The brand's animated mark - a signal dot with radiating pulse rings.
components.css: .ds-pin { position: relative; display: inline-flex; width: 40px; height: 40px; align-items: center; justify-content: center; } .ds-pin-dot { width: 12px; height: 12px; background: #FF4D23; border-radius: 9999px; z-index: 1; } .ds-pin-ring { position: absolute; width: 12px; height: 12px; border-radius: 9999px; background: rgba(255,77,35,0.4); animation: ds-pin-pulse 2.4s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1) infinite; } @keyframes ds-pin-pulse { 0% { transform: scale(0.6); opacity: 0.9; } 70% { transform: scale(2.4); opacity: 0; } 100% { transform: scale(2.4); opacity: 0; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-pin-ring { animation: none; opacity: 0; } }

narrative.overview: LeadZipp looks like a working map spread on a good desk: warm paper with a fine grain, topographic contours in deep forest green, and one bright beacon pin that marks where to go next. The system is warm and confident - a well-made physical tool, not a tech demo. Light surfaces are cream paper with ink text; dark sections flip into the map world of deep greens with contour lines, where the beacon orange and a rare electric lime read like markings on a night chart. Interactions are tactile and alive: cards lift on hover, buttons press down a pixel on click, map pins pulse.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground (#FBFAF6) with ink text - never sterile white/gray
Cartographic motifs: topo contours, dot-grid, pulsing pins, mono readouts
One voice of accent: signal red-orange, earned and rare
Dark sections are deep map-green, not black
Tactile motion: lift, press, pulse - 220ms with a soft spring curve

rules.name: The Two Oranges Rule
rules.body: Signal (#C22F0A) on light surfaces; Signal Bright (#FF4D23) on dark forest surfaces only. Never swap them, never unify them - the split exists for WCAG AA contrast.

rules.name: The One Beacon Rule
rules.body: The accent appears where action or signal lives - one clear beacon per viewport, not orange everywhere.

rules.name: The Readout Rule
rules.body: Data fragments (counts, scores, ZIPs, coordinates) render in the mono readout style, not in body type - the map's instrument voice.

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow derives from Ink, not black or gray - depth stays inside the paper world.

dos: Do put grain/dot-grid/topo texture behind sections - it is the brand's ground.
Do use the mono readout voice for any datum (scores, counts, ZIPs).
Do keep motion physical and brief: 200-220ms, spring curve, lift/press/pulse.
donts: Don't mix the two oranges across surface types (The Two Oranges Rule).
Don't introduce pure white/gray/black grounds - every neutral is warm.
Don't use gray or black shadows - shadows derive from Ink.
Don't fabricate proof (logos, counts, testimonials) - zero customers today; evidence lives in PRODUCT.md.
Don't load Google Fonts at build time - fonts are self-hosted woff2.
